disease_label_per_paper: Meningococcaemia causing necrotizing cellulitis associated with acquired complement deficiency after gastric bypass surgery
presentation_summary: 50-year-old woman with prior complicated gastric bypass, severe malnutrition requiring enteral supplement, hypertension and discoid lupus presented with septic shock and necrotizing cellulitis due to Neisseria meningitidis serogroup W.
A few hours before admission she developed sudden intense leg pain and malaise; emergency room exam showed hyperemia and swelling of both anterior thighs and right abdominal flank.
Admission vitals: blood pressure 50/35 mmHg, heart rate 140/min, temperature 35.3 C, lactate 12 mmol/L.
Septic shock was associated with severe DIC: PT 30 s, APTT >150 s, platelets 6000/mm3, D-dimers 25000 mcg/L, fibrinogen 85 mg/dL; AKI with creatinine 2 mg/dL, urea 96 mg/dL and oliguria 20 mL/h.
Urgent surgical exploration showed extensive subcutaneous necrosis not involving fascia; all surgical samples and blood cultures returned positive for Neisseria meningitidis serogroup W.
